title: Game Instructions
introduction: The complete Kaiser XI manual, from creating a League through troubleshooting.
details: How it works

gettingStarted.title: First Steps
gettingStarted.overview: Kaiser XI is a fantasy football game for private and customizable leagues with your friends. Create your account, open the dashboard, and get started by creating a new league or joining an existing one via invitation.
details: In Kaiser XI, each participant manages a fantasy team made up of real-life soccer players. Throughout the season, the performances of these players determine the fantasy teams' points and thus the course of the competition.
First, create an account with your name, email address, and a password. After logging in, the dashboard is your starting point for accessing your leagues and the app's main features.

If you want to organize a new competition with your friends, create a league. You will become the Commissioner and can configure the rules, invite other participants, and prepare for the championship.
If someone else has already created the league, you can join via invitation. You will then be a member of the league and can manage your assigned fantasy team.
Each league can be configured differently. Before you start playing, you should therefore read the league rules and familiarize yourself with the settings chosen by the Commissioner.
gettingStarted.callout: Each group can create their own player experience by selecting a league type and configuring the desired rules.

creatingLeague.title: Creating a League
creatingLeague.overview: A League is a private competitive space where you can play with your friends. The person who creates it becomes the Commissioner and defines its main characteristics and initial rules.
details: Enter a name for the League and, if you want, an optional description. Then select the Competition/Season you want to play: the League will use the players, matches and Matchdays belonging to the selected season.

Choose the League type between Classic, Head-to-Head and Formula One. In Classic, the points earned by Fantasy Teams across the different Matchdays are added together. In Head-to-Head, Fantasy Teams face each other directly: the fantasy score is converted into goals and determines wins, draws and losses. In Formula One, Fantasy Teams are ranked on each Matchday according to their score and receive points based on their finishing position.

Set the maximum number of participants, from 2 to 100. This determines how many people can take part in the League. For an easier-to-manage playing experience, it is generally recommended not to exceed around 12 participants.
Set the initial budget. The default value is 500 credits and represents the starting funds available to each Fantasy Team for managing its squad.

Configure the release refund percentage, maximum squad size and limits for goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders and forwards. The release refund percentage is explained in more detail in the Market section.

Once the League has been created, you become its Commissioner. Kaiser XI automatically adds the default rules, but the League setup is not yet complete: you will need to invite the participants, review and optionally adjust the rules, create and assign the Fantasy Teams, and register the initial squads.
creatingLeague.callout: Creating and configuring the League is the Commissioner's responsibility. Before starting the championship, make sure that participants, Fantasy Teams, squads and rules have all been configured correctly.

buildingSquads.title: Building the Initial Squads
buildingSquads.overview: Before the championship begins, the participants must decide which players belong to each Fantasy Team. Kaiser XI does not manage this phase directly: you can organize it however you prefer, and the Commissioner will then enter the agreed squads into the app.
details: Traditional auction: a player is nominated and participants place their bids. The highest bidder acquires the player for the winning price. This is the most traditional method and makes the initial budget particularly important.

Sealed bids: each participant prepares their offers without knowing the bids made by the others. At the agreed deadline, the bids are compared and each player is assigned according to the rules established by the group, normally to the highest bidder.
Draft: participants take turns selecting an available player according to a predefined order. With this system, the budget may be less important depending on the rules chosen by the group.
Whichever method you choose, each Fantasy Team must have a defined squad at the end of the process. The Commissioner can then assign the players to their respective teams in Kaiser XI.
This phase concerns only the creation of the initial squads. The in-season Market and Trades between Fantasy Teams are separate features.
buildingSquads.callout: Before starting, make sure all participants agree on the player allocation method and its rules. Kaiser XI records the resulting squads but does not run the auction, sealed bids or draft.

leagueOverview.title: Understanding Your League
leagueOverview.overview: The League page is the starting point for following the championship and accessing all of its sections. From here you can view Fantasy Teams, League Rules, the Market, Matchdays, standings and the other features available in your League.
details: Fantasy Teams: here you can find all Fantasy Teams participating in the League. You can view their owners, squads and the main information about each team.

League Rules: contains the rules used by the League, including squad composition, allowed formations, bench rules, substitutions, bonuses and penalties, as well as any rules specific to the selected League type.
Market: this section is used to manage players during the season. When the Market is available, you can view players and manage signings and releases according to the League configuration.
Matchdays: lets you follow the different Matchdays of the season. From here you can access formations, scores and available results for each Matchday.
Standings: shows the progress of the championship. How the standings work depends on the selected League type: Classic, Head-to-Head or Formula One.
Calendar: in Head-to-Head Leagues, this shows the scheduled fixtures between Fantasy Teams.
Your Fantasy Team: from your team you can check your squad and prepare your formation for each Matchday. The following sections of this guide explain squad, formation and bench management in detail.

The Commissioner also has access to the functions required to administer the League, manage participants and configure the championship. These operations are explained in the dedicated Commissioner section.
leagueOverview.callout: Use the League page as the central point for navigating all championship activities. Some sections or actions may become available only when the League reaches the required stage.

leagueRules.title: League Rules
leagueRules.overview: League Rules define how the competition is played: squad composition, allowed formations, bench, substitutions, bonuses, penalties and settings specific to the selected League type.
details: Squads and budget: the Commissioner can configure the initial budget, the release refund percentage, the maximum squad size and the limits for goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders and forwards. These values determine which squad operations are considered valid.
Formations: the League defines which formations can be used, the bench size and the role limits for bench players. A formation can only be submitted if it complies with the configured rules.

Substitutions: the Commissioner can define the maximum number of substitutions and the criteria used to select players from the bench. Depending on the configuration, substitutions may need to preserve the original formation or may allow switching to another permitted formation.

Bonuses and penalties: the League can assign different values to events recorded for a player, such as goals, assists, cards, own goals, penalties scored or missed, penalties saved and goals conceded. These values contribute to the player's fantasy score.
Additional bonuses: if enabled, specific bonuses can be applied, such as the real captain bonus and the goalkeeper clean-sheet bonus.

Defense modifier: if enabled, the team score can receive an additional bonus based on the ratings of the goalkeeper and the best defenders in the lineup, according to the thresholds configured in the League.

League-type-specific rules: in Head-to-Head Leagues, the Commissioner configures the thresholds used to convert fantasy points into goals. In Formula One Leagues, the Commissioner instead configures how many championship points are awarded for each Matchday finishing position.
Market and Trades: League Rules also include settings related to Market and Trade availability, such as opening and closing times and whether credit adjustments can be used in Trades.
leagueRules.callout: Before the championship begins, review all League Rules carefully. Some settings may become restricted after squads have been created or the competition has started, in order to prevent configurations that are incompatible with the current League state.

championship.title: Championship Configuration
championship.overview: Once participants, Fantasy Teams, squads and rules are ready, the Commissioner can configure and initialize the championship. This step prepares the competition and determines how the Matchdays of the selected Season will be used.
details: Before configuring the championship, make sure that all participants have accepted their invitations and that each of them has been assigned a Fantasy Team. At least two Fantasy Teams must be present, and the League squads and rules should already have been reviewed.

Choose the future Matchday from which the championship should begin. Earlier Matchdays will not be part of the League competition, while the available Matchdays starting from the selected one will be used as the championship progresses.

In Classic Leagues, the scores earned by Fantasy Teams are recorded starting from the selected Matchday. Scores from the different Matchdays are progressively added together to determine the standings.
In Formula One Leagues, the available future Matchdays are used. On each Matchday, Fantasy Teams are ranked according to their score and receive the position points defined in the League Rules.

In Head-to-Head Leagues, the Commissioner also configures the number of round robins. Kaiser XI uses the available future Matchdays to create the fixture calendar between Fantasy Teams, so enough Matchdays must be available to complete the selected format.

Review all settings carefully before initializing the championship. Initialization marks the transition from League preparation to the actual competition and should not be confused with simply creating the League.
championship.callout: Check participants, Fantasy Teams, squads, rules and the starting Matchday. For a Head-to-Head League, also make sure that enough Matchdays are available to generate all required fixtures.

squadSetup.title: Initial Squad Setup
squadSetup.overview: After completing the auction, sealed bids or draft, the Commissioner must record the agreed squads in Kaiser XI by assigning each player to the correct Fantasy Team.
details: First, make sure that all Fantasy Teams have been created and assigned to the correct participants. Every League member should have their own Fantasy Team before the championship begins.

Open the Fantasy Team you want to configure and assign the players obtained during the initial squad-building process. For each player, also enter the agreed purchase price when this applies to the allocation method used by your group.
The purchase price is deducted from the Fantasy Team's available budget. For example, with an initial budget of 500 credits and total purchases of 430 credits, 70 credits remain available.

During assignment, Kaiser XI checks that the squad complies with the League Rules, including available budget, maximum squad size and role limits. The same player cannot belong to two Fantasy Teams in the same League at the same time.

Repeat the process for every Fantasy Team and compare the result with what was agreed during the auction, sealed bids or draft. Before starting the championship, verify that every team contains the correct players and that budgets and role limits are respected.
Initial Squad Setup only records the result of the player-allocation phase in Kaiser XI. It does not automatically open the Market and it does not replace the later championship initialization.
squadSetup.callout: Configure every squad carefully before initializing the championship. Correcting players, prices or assignments at this stage is much easier than making changes after the competition has already started.

market.title: Market
market.overview: The Market allows Fantasy Teams to propose player trades during the periods established by the Commissioner. Trades must comply with the League Rules and the squad restrictions of the teams involved.
details: The Commissioner decides whether the Market is active and configures its opening and closing period. Trades can only be proposed while the Market is open.
During the Market, you can propose a trade to another Fantasy Team in the League by offering one of your players and requesting one of their players in return.

The players involved do not necessarily need to have the same role. A trade is possible as long as, once completed, both Fantasy Teams continue to comply with the squad size and role limits defined in the League Rules.

For example, you can propose trading a defender for a midfielder if, after the trade, both Fantasy Teams still comply with their respective defender and midfielder limits. If either squad would exceed a League limit, the trade would not be valid.

The Commissioner can decide whether credit adjustments are also allowed. When this option is enabled, in addition to exchanging players you can offer credits or request credits from the receiving Fantasy Team.
Example: you offer player A in exchange for player B. If credit adjustments are enabled, you can offer A + 10 credits for B, or request A in exchange for B + 10 credits.

Sending a proposal does not immediately modify the squads. The trade is completed only when the proposal is accepted and all required conditions are valid. At that point, the players and any credit adjustment are transferred between the two Fantasy Teams.
Before proposing or accepting a trade, check the composition of both squads, their role limits, the available budget when credits are involved and the League Rules.
market.callout: A trade can also involve players with different roles. What matters is that, after the Trade, both Fantasy Teams continue to comply with the squad and individual role limits established by the League.

fantasyTeam.title: Your Fantasy Team
fantasyTeam.overview: The Fantasy Team page brings together all the information about your team: owner, available budget and the players in your squad.
details: Each League participant has a Fantasy Team. From this page, you can check your squad composition and the main information about your team.
The squad contains all players assigned to the Fantasy Team. For each player, you can see key information such as their role and the purchase price recorded during the initial squad setup.

The budget shows how many credits are currently available. Its initial value depends on the League Rules and is reduced by the prices of the players assigned to the squad. During the season, it can also change as a result of Trades that include a credit adjustment.

Your Fantasy Team squad does not automatically represent the Formation used for a Matchday. Before each Matchday, you must select the starters and bench players from your squad while respecting the League Rules. From your Fantasy Team page, you can also change its name and personalize it as you prefer.

During the Market, the composition of your Fantasy Team can change through Trades completed with other teams. After a Trade, always check your updated squad and available budget before preparing your next Formation.
fantasyTeam.callout: Your squad contains all players belonging to your Fantasy Team. Your Formation is the selection of starters and substitutes you choose for a specific Matchday.

formation.title: Formation
formation.overview: For each Matchday, choose the Formation your Fantasy Team will use: select the formation, the 11 starters and the bench before the deadline.
details: Open the Formation section for the Matchday you want to play. You can create and modify your Formation until the Matchday begins; after the deadline, it can no longer be saved or submitted.

Choose one of the formations allowed by the League Rules. The selected formation determines how many defenders, midfielders and forwards must be fielded, while the goalkeeper always occupies the goalkeeper position.
Select exactly 11 starters from your squad while respecting the chosen formation. A player selected as a starter cannot also be included on the bench.

Then complete the bench according to the required number of substitutes and any role limits defined in the League Rules. The order of the players on the bench can be important for determining automatic substitutions.

You can save the Formation as a draft and continue modifying it until the deadline. Once you are satisfied with your choices, submit it to confirm it: only a correctly submitted Formation is used when calculating the Matchday.

If you change the formation after already selecting your starters, Kaiser XI asks you to confirm the change. If confirmed, the starters are removed because they may no longer be compatible with the new formation, while the bench is preserved. You can then select your 11 starters again.

At the end of the Matchday, if one of your starters cannot contribute to the score, Kaiser XI attempts to replace that player automatically with a valid player from the bench. The maximum number and substitution criteria depend on the League Rules.

Substitutions can follow the bench order or role priority, depending on the League settings. If formation changes during substitutions are not allowed, the final Formation must preserve the original formation; if they are allowed, substitutions may result in another formation permitted by the League.
If no valid substitute can replace a starter, the substitution is not made and that player does not contribute to the Fantasy Team's score.
formation.callout: Saving your Formation as a draft is not the same as submitting it. Before the deadline, check your formation, starters, bench and substitute order, then confirm your Formation.

matchdays.title: Matchdays
matchdays.overview: Matchdays represent the individual rounds of the competition. From this section, you can follow the current Matchday and review those that have already been played.
details: Each Matchday corresponds to a round of the Season on which the League is based. Before it begins, you can prepare and submit your Fantasy Team's Formation before the deadline.
During the Matchday, you can follow the status of the round and, when available, view information related to Formations and scores.
After the Matchday has been calculated, you can view the results of the Fantasy Teams, their scores and the details of the Formations that were used.
Past Matchdays remain available as part of the League history. You can go back and review results, scores and Formations from previously completed Matchdays.
Where supported by the League view, you can also inspect the Formations and results of other Fantasy Teams, not only your own.
matchdays.callout: Use the Matchdays section to follow the current round and review what happened in previous Matchdays.

scoring.title: Scoring
scoring.overview: A Fantasy Team's score is based on the real performances of the players in its lineup. Kaiser XI starts from each player's base rating, applies the bonuses and penalties defined by the League Rules, and counts only the players who effectively contribute to the final Formation.
details: The starting point is the player's base rating, which represents the evaluation of their performance in the real match. The ratings used by Kaiser XI are derived from multiple recognized public football sources and are combined to obtain a reference value.

Bonuses and penalties are then applied to the base rating according to the events recorded during the real match. Supported events include goals, assists, yellow and red cards, own goals, penalties scored, penalties missed, penalties saved and goals conceded.

With the default values, a goal is worth +3 points, an assist +1, a yellow card −0.5, a red card −1, an own goal −2, a scored penalty +3, a missed penalty −3, a saved penalty +3 and a goal conceded −1. The Commissioner can change these values through the League Rules.

A player's fantasy score is therefore the base rating plus the applicable bonuses and penalties. For example, a player with a 6.5 rating who scores a goal, provides an assist and receives a yellow card scores, with the default values: 6.5 + 3 + 1 − 0.5 = 10 points.
Only players who are part of the effective Formation after substitutions are considered for the Fantasy Team score. Players who remain unused on the bench do not contribute to the total.

If a starter cannot contribute and is validly replaced by a bench player, the substitute contributes to the Fantasy Team total instead. If no valid substitution is available, that position produces no points.

Optional League bonuses can also be added to individual player performances. The captain bonus is applied when the corresponding rule is enabled and the contributing player is recorded as the real captain. A goalkeeper may also receive a clean-sheet bonus when that option is enabled and the required conditions are met.

If the defense modifier is enabled, Kaiser XI evaluates the goalkeeper and defenders who effectively contribute to the Formation. A valid goalkeeper and at least four defenders are required. The goalkeeper's base rating and the three highest defender base ratings are averaged, and the applicable bonus is determined by the thresholds configured in the League.

Defense modifier example: the goalkeeper has a rating of 6.0 and the three highest-rated defenders have 6.5, 7.0 and 6.5. The average is (6.0 + 6.5 + 7.0 + 6.5) / 4 = 6.5. If the League Rules award +2 points at the 6.5 threshold, the Fantasy Team receives an additional 2-point bonus.

The Fantasy Team total is the sum of the scores contributed by the effective Formation plus any applicable team bonuses. This total is then used differently depending on the League type: Classic, Head-to-Head or Formula One.

Always check your League Rules before a Matchday. Two Leagues using the same players and the same real-world ratings can produce different fantasy results if their coefficients, bonuses or modifiers are configured differently.
scoring.callout: The base rating represents the player's real performance, but the fantasy result depends on the League Rules. Bonuses, penalties, captain, clean sheet and the defense modifier can all affect the final score.

results.title: Results, Standings and Calendar
results.overview: After a Matchday has been calculated, you can view the Fantasy Team results and detailed scores. The standings use these results differently depending on the League type: Classic, Head-to-Head or Formula One.
details: The Matchday results show the total score achieved by each Fantasy Team and allow you to inspect the Formation used. This lets you see which players contributed to the result and which substitutions were applied.

The result details allow you to reconstruct the Fantasy Team's score by showing the contributions of individual players and any bonuses defined by the League Rules. For an explanation of how these values are calculated, see the Scoring chapter.

In Classic Leagues, the fantasy scores earned across the different Matchdays are added together. The overall standings therefore rank Fantasy Teams according to the total fantasy points accumulated during the season.

In Head-to-Head Leagues, each Matchday places two Fantasy Teams against each other. Each team's fantasy score is converted into goals according to the thresholds configured in the League Rules and determines a win, draw or loss. The standings track the match results and the corresponding statistics.
Head-to-Head Leagues also include a Calendar where you can view the scheduled fixtures between Fantasy Teams across the different Matchdays and follow the progress of the championship.

In Formula One Leagues, Fantasy Teams are ranked on each Matchday according to their fantasy score. Each position receives the number of points defined in the League Rules, and the overall standings accumulate the position points earned throughout the season.

You can return to previous Matchdays to review already calculated results and Formations. Together, results, standings and the calendar allow you to follow and reconstruct the complete history of the League.
results.calloutLabel: The League type determines the standings
results.callout: The fantasy score is calculated within the same game context, but each League format uses it differently: it is accumulated in Classic, converted into a match result in Head-to-Head and converted into position points in Formula One.

calculation.title: Calculate and Recalculate
calculation.overview: At the end of a Matchday, the Commissioner can start the calculation of the League results. If data affecting the scores is later corrected or updated, the Matchday may need to be recalculated.
details: The Commissioner can calculate a Matchday once it has ended and the data required to determine the scores is available.

When Calculate is selected, Kaiser XI determines which players contribute to the Formations, applies any required substitutions and calculates the scores using ratings, bonuses, penalties and the League Rules.

Once the calculation is complete, the Matchday results are generated and the information required for the standings is updated. The final outcome depends on the League type: Classic, Head-to-Head or Formula One.

A Matchday that has already been calculated does not change automatically if data used for its score is later corrected. For example, if a player's rating is corrected from 6.5 to 7.0, the published result remains unchanged until the Matchday is recalculated.

In these situations, the Commissioner can use Recalculate. Kaiser XI calculates the Matchday again using the data and League Rules available at that time and updates the scores, results and standings accordingly.

Recalculation may therefore be necessary when ratings, bonuses, penalties or other data affecting the Matchday result are corrected. There is no need to recalculate a Matchday when no relevant data used by the calculation has changed.
Before recalculating an already published Matchday, remember that its results and the standings may change. This function should therefore be used only when a correction is actually required.
calculation.callout: Calculate is used to generate the results of a Matchday. Recalculate is used to update an already calculated Matchday when data that can affect its result has been changed or corrected.

commissioner.title: Commissioner Guide
commissioner.overview: The Commissioner is responsible for managing the League. They create and configure the competition, invite participants, manage Fantasy Teams and League Rules, and oversee the League throughout the season.
details: When you create a League, you automatically become its Commissioner. Before inviting other participants, carefully check the Season, League type, maximum number of participants and League Rules.

Invite participants to the League and make sure that every member has their own Fantasy Team. The Commissioner can manage members and their Fantasy Teams through the administrative tools available in the League.

After completing the initial player allocation through an auction, sealed bids, draft or another method agreed upon by the group, register the squads in Kaiser XI. Carefully check players, prices, budgets and squad limits before proceeding.

Before the competition begins, configure the championship. Make sure that all participants and Fantasy Teams are ready and that the League Rules are final, then initialize the competition. Some settings can no longer be freely changed after this point.

Manage the League Rules throughout the season. Among other things, they determine Formations, the bench, substitutions, bonuses and penalties, modifiers and how results are calculated. Before changing them, always consider the impact on future Matchdays.
Manage the Market by deciding whether it is enabled and setting its opening and closing period. Where supported, you can also allow credit adjustments in trades between Fantasy Teams.

Remind participants about important deadlines, especially those for submitting Formations and using the Market. Clear communication of the Rules and deadlines helps prevent most problems during the season.

At the end of a Matchday, once the required data is available, use Calculate to generate scores and results. If data affecting an already calculated Matchday is later corrected, use Recalculate only when necessary.

Before making important changes, initializing the competition or recalculating an already published Matchday, always consider the consequences for all participants. The Commissioner has more management tools than other members and is therefore responsible for keeping the League consistent and understandable.
commissioner.callout: Before the season begins, check participants, Fantasy Teams, squads and League Rules. During the competition, communicate deadlines, manage the Market and use Calculate and Recalculate carefully.

profile.title: Profile and Personalization
profile.overview: From the Profile section, you can manage your account information and personalize the appearance of Kaiser XI by choosing your language and color palette.
details: You can update your profile information, such as your name and email address. These changes affect only your account and do not modify your Fantasy Team or the Leagues you participate in.
You can change your account password. For security reasons, your current password and confirmation of the new password are required.

Kaiser XI is available in Italian, English and German. Changing the language translates the interface and Game Instructions, while user-created content, such as League or Fantasy Team names and descriptions, remains unchanged.
You can personalize the appearance of the app by choosing from different football-inspired color palettes. The selected palette changes colors, backgrounds, buttons and other interface elements.
Language and palette are personal preferences. Each user can choose their preferred combination without changing the experience of other participants.
Profile settings do not modify the League Rules, scores, Formations, Market, standings or any other game data.
profile.callout: Language and palette affect only your experience in the app. Other participants can use different settings without affecting the League.

faq.title: FAQ and Troubleshooting
faq.overview: Here you can find answers to the most common issues you may encounter while using Kaiser XI.
details: Why can't I submit my Formation? Check that the Matchday has not already started, that you are editing your own Fantasy Team, that the selected formation is allowed and that starters and bench comply with the League Rules. Also remember that saving a draft is not the same as submitting the Formation.

Why did my starters disappear after changing formation? If you change formation after selecting starters, Kaiser XI asks for confirmation. If you confirm, the starters are cleared because they may no longer be compatible with the new formation, while the bench is preserved.
Why can't I find a specific formation? Each League can decide which formations are allowed. If a formation is not available, it has not been enabled in the League Rules.

Why can't I propose a Trade? Make sure the Market is open and that the proposal complies with the League Rules. After the Trade, both Fantasy Teams must still respect squad size and role limits. If a credit adjustment is included, sufficient budget must also be available.
What happens when a Trade proposal expires? An expired proposal can no longer be accepted, rejected or cancelled and does not modify the players or budgets of either Fantasy Team.

Why didn't a corrected player rating change an already published result? Calculated Matchdays are not rewritten automatically. If a correction affects the result, the Commissioner must use Recalculate.

Why can't the Commissioner initialize the championship? Before initialization, the League requirements must be satisfied, including the required Fantasy Teams and a valid future Matchday. Head-to-Head Leagues also require enough Matchdays to generate the fixture calendar.

What happens if one of my starters does not play? Kaiser XI attempts to apply a substitution using the bench and the League Rules. If no valid substitution exists, that player will not contribute to the score.

Why wasn't a bench player used? The player may not have been valid for the substitution, may have been beyond the maximum number of substitutions or may not have allowed a Formation compatible with the League Rules.
Why didn't I receive the defense modifier? The modifier must be enabled and its conditions must be met, including a valid goalkeeper and at least four defenders contributing to the Formation.
Why didn't my goalkeeper receive the clean-sheet bonus? The bonus must be enabled in the League Rules and the goalkeeper must effectively contribute to the Formation with a recorded clean sheet.
faq.callout: If you cannot find the answer you need here, visit the Kaiser XI community forum to ask questions, talk with other players and browse existing discussions.
